title: SEG Edge Base Definitions
description: Shared $defs referenced by all edge type schemas in the Safety Evidence Graph. Not used directly — import via $ref from individual edge schemas.

hashObject.description: A SHA256 hash value. Used for edgeHash fields.

hashValue.description: Lowercase hex-encoded SHA256 digest. Must be exactly 64 characters.

baseEdge.description: Fields common to all edge types.

id.description: Globally unique IRI for this edge record. Form: {namespaceBase}/edge/{edgeType}/{fromId}-{toId}. Maps to spdxId on SPDX export.

type.description: Fixed SEG edge type. One of: seg:Refines, seg:Verifies, seg:Implements, seg:Confirms, seg:Witnesses, seg:Excuses, seg:Calls.

seg:from.description: IRI of the source node. Must resolve to an existing node in the graph. Cross-node validation is enforced at graph level, not schema level.

seg:to.description: IRI of the target node. Must resolve to an existing node in the graph. Cross-node validation is enforced at graph level, not schema level.

strongEdge.description: Additional fields required on strong-propagation edges (refines, verifies, implements). These edges carry suspicion propagation and require human affirmation to resolve. Provenance of affirmation (who affirmed, when) is derived from git log in repo G — not stored in the edge record.

seg:edgeHash.description: Hash computed as H(from || to || type || nodeHash(from) || nodeHash(to)) at the time of last affirmation. Cryptographically binds the edge to the content of both endpoints at the moment a human affirmed the relationship. The suspect link detector recomputes this hash using current node hashes — a mismatch marks the edge suspect.

seg:linkState.description: Current integrity state of this edge. pending: edge exists but has never been affirmed (initial bootstrap state). active: both endpoints unchanged since last affirmation. directlyOutdated: this node's own content changed. transitivelySuspect: a dependency changed. doublyOutdated: both this node and a dependency changed. broken: one or both endpoint nodes no longer exist in their source repository — cannot be resolved by affirmation. Only active edges contribute to a valid proof. All other states block proof generation.
